scope: Theorem 3.1 (The presentation comparison theorem) of the manuscript “A finitely generated counterexample to the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture” (preprints/A-finitely-generated-counterexample-to-the-Eilenberg-Ganea-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 249 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 bbc781ac6f173938), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose that Γ is residually finite and that D is a finite indexed list of words on S, trivial in Γ, whose chains form a free Λ-basis of ker ∂1. Thus the canonical map Λ(D) −→ ker ∂1, ez ⟼ [z], (3.1) is an isomorphism. If Γ admits a K(Γ, 1) of dimension at most two, there is an η > 0 with the following property. Assign a label in H = SU(2) to every oriented generator edge, assign the inverse label to its reverse, and assume that every label has distance less than η from 1. If the product along every translate of every z ∈ D is 1, then the product along every closed edge path is 1.
